spatial_claims.claim: Two concentric circles about center A; BCDE is the greater circle, FGHK is the lesser circle
BD is a diameter of the greater circle through center A, so B, A, D are collinear with B and D on the circle
AC is drawn perpendicular to BD at A and produced to E; CE is a diameter perpendicular to BD
BCDE forms a square inscribed in the greater circle; four arcs BC, CD, DE, EB are equal quadrants, so four chords are equal
L is the foot of the perpendicular from A to BC; AL is perpendicular to BC; if BC touches or intersects the lesser circle then AL is at most AF (radius of lesser circle)
M is the midpoint of arc BC; bisecting all arcs gives eight equal arcs forming a regular octagon inscribed in the greater circle
AN is the perpendicular distance from A to chord BM; BM subtends a smaller arc than BC, so BM is a shorter chord, hence further from center; therefore AN > AL
If AN > AF (radius of lesser circle), no side of the octagon touches the lesser circle because the minimum distance from A to each side exceeds AF
At each bisection from a 2^k-gon to a 2^(k+1)-gon, the perpendicular distance from A to each side strictly increases and the residual (AB minus perpendicular distance) decreases by more than half
After sufficiently many bisections (by 10.1), the perpendicular distance from A to each side exceeds AF
Every point on a side of the polygon is at distance from A at least equal to the perpendicular distance from A to that side; since this exceeds AF, no side touches the lesser circle

configuration_map: Center A is the common center of both circles throughout. The greater circle has radius AB and passes through B, C, D, E. The lesser circle has radius AF and passes through F, G, H, K. B and D are diametrically opposite on the greater circle, with A the midpoint of BD. C and E are diametrically opposite on the greater circle, with CE perpendicular to BD at A. These four points form a square BCDE. L is the foot of the perpendicular from A to chord BC, lying on BC at its midpoint (by the symmetry of the inscribed square). M is the midpoint of arc BC, lying on the greater circle between B and C. N is the foot of the perpendicular from A to chord BM, lying on BM. At each stage of bisection, new vertices are placed at arc midpoints on the greater circle, and the perpendicular distance from A to each new (shorter) chord increases monotonically. All constructed points remain consistently positioned throughout the proof.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The concentric circle configuration is maintained throughout. The key geometric relationship — that bisecting arcs produces shorter chords which are further from the center (by III.15), thereby increasing the perpendicular distance from A to each side — is correctly established and consistently applied. The application of X.1 to show the residual eventually becomes less than AB - AF is valid because each bisection reduces the residual by more than half (verifiable by the identity 1 - cos(theta) < (1 - cos(2*theta))/2 for relevant angles). No step's spatial assumptions contradict any other step's spatial assumptions.
